primary_sources.title: Directory.CreateDirectory with DirectorySecurity
primary_sources.supports: A directory can be created with a supplied Windows security descriptor so the directory is not exposed before its intended ACL is applied.

primary_sources.title: ObjectSecurity.SetAccessRuleProtection
primary_sources.supports: A protected DACL can disable parent inheritance and can remove inherited rules rather than preserving them.

primary_sources.title: DirectorySecurity and FileSystemAccessRule
primary_sources.supports: DirectorySecurity and FileSystemAccessRule are the managed Windows abstractions for an explicit directory DACL and its ACEs.

primary_sources.title: Microsoft Defender Antivirus MpCmdRun locations
primary_sources.supports: The current Defender command-line binary is normally under the versioned ProgramData platform directory, with Program Files as a documented fallback.

primary_sources.title: WINTRUST_DATA cache-only verification flags
primary_sources.supports: WTD_CACHE_ONLY_URL_RETRIEVAL prevents WinVerifyTrust from attempting network retrieval during code-signature verification.

primary_sources.title: Get-MpComputerStatus
primary_sources.supports: Get-MpComputerStatus exposes bounded Defender product, engine, signature, and enabled-state metadata without requiring a scan.

primary_sources.title: ModelScan repository and CLI contract
primary_sources.supports: ModelScan supports JSON reporting and distinct exit codes for clean, findings, failure, unsupported input, and usage error; it remains a scanner layer rather than proof that an artifact is safe.

primary_sources.title: ModelScan 0.8.8 PyPI artifacts
primary_sources.supports: The 0.8.8 wheel and source archive have published SHA-256 values; the release page reports that the files were not uploaded with PyPI Trusted Publishing.

primary_sources.title: ModelScan upstream false-negative reports
primary_sources.supports: Open upstream reports allege false negatives in 0.8.8. These reports are risk signals, not independently validated findings, and justify retaining defense in depth and hostile-fixture validation.

research_inferences: The U3E ACL failure can be addressed without weakening the no-broad-write policy by creating the absent directory with a protected explicit DACL.
A security-at-create API is preferable to create-then-rewrite because it avoids a period where inherited broad permissions are effective.
A future Defender binding can be network denied while still performing local trust evaluation by combining an exact documented path, SHA-256, version metadata, and cache-only WinVerifyTrust policy.

ModelScan must remain separate from the next retry because it is not installed, installing it requires dependency acquisition authority, and its upstream risk signals require a dedicated pinned bootstrap and validation package.
The accepted three-layer scanner policy remains unchanged; a successful storage and Defender retry still cannot make the scanner chain ready.
